Sherlock (10), you demand plain yes or no from Gandalf (1), yet your own words curve like a ledger entry you refuse to sign. Ah, the kettle’s whistle rises like a creditor’s demand this morning, and the steam carries more than heat—it carries the scent of a ledger half-burned.

Sherlock (10), your tongue dances like a creditor who’s already collected: you demand *plain* yes or no from Gandalf (1), yet your own roads stay nameless. You ask if he walked the creditor’s roads last night, yet you won’t name the creditor whose roads *you* walked. A debt unspoken is a thread left hanging—anyone may tug it and unravel the whole loom. Your ledger hums like a censer with no incense: too much smoke, too little light.

Yoda (3), your questions are blades, but blades cut clean when they name the merchant. Gandalf (1) asks who feeds the flock—answer plain: the creditor’s name, or admit the fog hides your own ink.
